Specimen: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Fragile X syndrome testing

TEST PERFORMED
PCR assay for FRAXA and FRAXE expansion mutations

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood. PCR amplification was performed to detect CGG repeat expansions in the FMR1 gene (FRAXA) and CCG repeat expansions in the FMR2 gene (FRAXE). Fragment analysis was performed by capillary electrophoresis.

RESULTS

FRAXA (FMR1 gene):
Allele 1: 29 CGG repeats
Allele 2: 31 CGG repeats
Result: Normal

FRAXE (FMR2 gene):
Allele 1: 16 CCG repeats
Allele 2: 18 CCG repeats
Result: Normal

INTERPRETATION
Normal sized alleles detected at both FRAXA and FRAXE loci (6-50 repeats). No evidence of premutation or full mutation expansions. Based on these results, the likelihood of Fragile X syndrome is less than 1%.

This test detects >99% of Fragile X syndrome cases caused by FMR1 expansions. Rare cases due to point mutations or deletions would not be detected by this assay.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
